raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 keeps the BF16 latent MoE up-projection replicated on every TP rank. For the 92 MoE layers with a `[7168, 3584]` weight, storing only one eighth on each TP8 rank saves **4,136,108,032 parameter bytes (3.852 GiB) per GPU**. Memory-constrained decode workers can use the freed budget for KV cache.

This is a memory optimization with a communication cost. The measured projection tail is slower at most batch sizes. Exact-version full-model and matched service experiments are now complete: code alone changes output throughput by **+2.24%** at MRR512 on the fixed 64K/1K workload below, with a latency tradeoff.

**This PR is open for review and CI; numerical acceptance remains unresolved.** The complete GSM8K evaluation passes the experiment's predeclared noninferiority criterion, but the stricter common-prefix logprob/top-1 gate fails. Numerical diagnosis isolates BF16 projection rounding after changing the GEMM output width. Performance results characterize the unchanged candidate; they do not resolve numerical acceptance or establish merge readiness.

## Modifications

- Use `ColumnParallelLinear` and its checkpoint loader for physical output-column sharding. Reuse `MultimemAllGatherer` to return the complete output on each rank; one workspace is shared across layers and keyed by the TP group.
- Enable the layout for CUDA decode workers with TP8, BF16 unquantized latent projections, hidden/latent widths 7168/3584, shared experts, no MoE A2A, no attention DP or layernorm SP, and the existing multicast-capable K3 fusion. Other configurations retain replicated weights. No new configuration flag.
- Keep the existing small-batch `gemm_ag` arithmetic. Its host entry accepts either the replicated weight or a local `[896, 3584]` shard and selects the local pointer before launch. The producer/consumer arithmetic and tail additions are unchanged.
- Larger batches use the existing gatherer's NCCL fallback. Keep ordinary prefill/mixed servers on the replicated layout because the gather cost is substantial for those batches.
- Extend the existing collective and parallel-placement tests.

Related work: #47075 and #44985 compute row slices of replicated up-projection weights on AMD; #45126 shards the latent **down/front** projection; #46474 tunes SM107 small-batch kernels and touches the same `gemm_ag` files. This PR changes physical up-weight storage on CUDA decode workers. Concurrent edits to the GEMV interface will need coordination.

## Accuracy Tests

Base: `2dc5bdd18b040d9ec0447743921edcbf7ba252f9`.

On 8×B300, PyTorch `2.14.1+cu130`, using the final six changed files:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_collectives.py \
  --num-gpu 8 -k 'gemm_all_gather or kimi_latent_up_projection' -q
```

**11 passed, 3 deselected** on each rank:

- GEMV batches 1/2/4/8/12, with and without the prefix addition. Replicated and local-shard outputs match bitwise; the output is also checked against an FP32 projection reference with BF16 tail rounding.
- Eager execution and five CUDA graph replays with changed inputs.
- Actual projection class and checkpoint loader: each rank receives its exact weight slice, with one eighth of the original physical parameter storage.
- Projection batches 0/1/12/13/219/267/512/513, including strided input and the multicast/NCCL boundary, checked against full `F.linear` in eager and graph modes.

CPU regression:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/layers/test_kimi_mlp_parallel_groups.py \
  test/registered/unit/layer_boundary/test_kimi_k3_stage_kernels.py -q
```

**9 passed, 28 subtests passed**. Placement checks construct the real MoE and linear layers on meta, reusing the existing router/expert fixtures. They cover eligible decode, prefill/mixed, TP4, CPU, FP16, EP/DP/SP, unavailable multicast, missing shared experts, other hidden widths, and non-latent models.

### Full model with real KV (2026-11-02)

Candidate: `3556b550983fabf788eb97b2a5a9ed545547a75a`; reference: the parent commit above. Both use complete, separately extracted source archives, checked file by file. Environment: 8×B300, TP8/DCP8/`fi_a2a`, BF16 KV/Mamba, PyTorch `2.14.1+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.7.1`.

The executor uses upstream `one_batch`/`ModelRunner` APIs with the real decode-mode construction, performs actual EXTEND prefill to populate KV/Mamba, then actual CUDA Graph DECODE. All eight ranks audit all 92 latent-up weights: `[7168,3584]` on the reference and physical `[896,3584]` shards on the candidate. No fake KV/transfer is used in this accuracy executor. This covers the complete model and state, not network P→D transfer.

139 diagnostic requests × 128 output tokens cover short bilingual/code/math chats, input boundaries 511/512/513, 8191/8192/8193, 16383/16384/16385 and 65536, plus batches 12/13/32/64. Compare independent greedy outputs and logprobs/top-1 on a shared reference continuation. Reference self-repeat is exact.

| Common-prefix metric (17,792 tokens) | Observed | Predeclared experiment criterion |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean absolute target logprob error | 0.015772 | ≤0.02, pass |
| P99 absolute target logprob error | 0.262677 | ≤0.2, **fail** |
| Maximum absolute target logprob error | 3.035137 | reported |
| Top-1 agreement | 98.8309% | ≥99%, **fail** |
| Exact free-greedy sequences | 60/139 | reported |

Batch 1/12/13 comparisons are exact; batches 32/64 differ. The prefill-produced first token agrees, and differences begin at the first Decode step. No nonfinite relevant logprobs or rank failures occurred.

Full **GSM8K test split (1319 questions)**, eight examples from TRAIN, greedy, batch 32, maximum 1024 output tokens:

| Metric | Reference | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Correct | 1259/1319 (95.4511%) | 1257/1319 (95.2995%) |
| Invalid answers | 2 | 1 |
| Capped outputs | 0 | 0 |

14 answers improve and 16 regress. Paired accuracy delta is **−0.1516 percentage points**, with a paired 20,000-resample bootstrap 95% CI of **[−0.9856,+0.6823] pp** (seed 42). This passes the predeclared lower bound of −2 pp. It does not establish quality for every model capability or long-context task.

**Numerical diagnosis:** eager and CUDA Graph results match within each version (12,288 tokens). All eight ranks verify that the gathered local output segment is bitwise identical to its local GEMM. On the same real activations, 368 layer/step projections have 0.189468% unequal full-versus-sharded BF16 elements, maximum absolute difference 0.015625. Rank 0 FP32-reference relative RMS errors are 0.165601947% (full) and 0.165601596% (sharded). Reconstructing full weights and substituting only full `F.linear` eliminates all full-model differences across 12,288 tokens. This isolates shape-dependent BF16 GEMM rounding, rather than gather, loading, or CUDA Graph errors. The intervention is diagnostic only: it is not a fix and is never used for performance measurements. The original strict gate remains failed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Matched projection + shared/prefix-add microbenchmark on 8×B300, BF16, CUDA graphs, without profiling. Both arms consume identical inputs. Rotate through 32 distinct weight matrices; take seven timing trials of 20 graph replays per arm. Each replay executes all 32 projections. Run reference→candidate, then candidate→reference. Report the slowest rank's median time per projection and tail, in microseconds.

| Batch | Replicated, round 1 / 2 (µs) | Sharded + gather, round 1 / 2 (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 | 10.960 / 10.954 | 17.115 / 17.067 |
| 219 | 16.081 / 16.078 | 21.807 / 21.636 |
| 251 | 16.707 / 16.689 | 22.472 / 22.359 |
| 267 | 19.155 / 19.127 | 22.657 / 22.639 |
| 384 | 22.680 / 24.125 | 26.184 / 25.676 |
| 512 | 28.827 / 28.866 | 29.256 / 28.764 |
| 513 | 31.392 / 31.592 | 63.678 / 63.645 |
| 4096 | 190.042 / 189.257 | 249.096 / 249.061 |

The 513/4096 rows directly exercise the projection's fallback to characterize its cost; normal prefill/mixed model construction retains the replicated layout. Batches ≤12 retain the existing fused GEMV path when eligible and are covered by correctness tests rather than this generic-projection timing table.

### Matched service experiments (same exact commits)

Four groups, two fresh services each: A=reference512, B=candidate512, D=reference272, C=candidate272, where the number is both MRR and maximum decode graph batch. Order A1/B1/B2/A2 then D1/C1/C2/D2. Each run has 512 warmup requests and 2048 formal requests, both at concurrency 512. Total 16,384 formal requests; warmup excluded.

aiakperf 1.6.3: fixed 65,536 input/1,024 output tokens, 16 client processes, seed 42, temperature 0, ignore EOS, streaming. Random input content does not mean random lengths. Common MF 0.97, context 69632, output reservation 1024, TP8/DCP8/fi_a2a, BF16 KV/Mamba, Radix disabled, extra slots 16, tokenizer/detokenizer 32. Fake-prefill decode throughput excludes real prefill and P/D network transfer.

All arms start with byte-identical complete baseline-only FlashInfer tactic caches, isolated writable/JIT caches, and the same input fingerprints. Cache hashes remain unchanged through measurement. A task-local aiakperf copy sets deterministic request IDs/bootstrap rooms and records input hashes before timing; upstream fake handoff hashes request IDs, so matching token lengths alone would not match requests. All 32 tokenizer workers are ready before formal timing. No profiling or diagnostic model hooks.

| Group | Round 1 / 2 output tok/s | Pooled output tok/s | P50 TTFT(s) | P99 TTFT(s) | Average TPOT(ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 3626.38 / 3629.99 | 3628.18 | 59.485 | 118.359 | 56.274 |
| B | 3715.29 / 3703.85 | 3709.56 | 63.741 | 127.298 | 60.815 |
| D | 3859.76 / 3836.64 | 3848.17 | 62.865 | 125.820 | 59.741 |
| C | 4020.70 / 4012.02 | 4016.35 | 65.930 | 67.150 | 63.196 |

Each pooled group contains 4096 successful requests. Throughput is total output tokens divided by summed formal durations. TTFT quantiles are recomputed from all raw requests in the group, not averaged across rounds.

| Comparison | Paired round 1 / 2 | Pooled throughput change |
|---|---:|---:|
| A→B: code only, MRR512 | +2.45% / +2.03% | +2.24% |
| A→D: capacity only, reference | +6.44% / +5.69% | +6.06% |
| B→C: capacity on candidate | +8.22% / +8.32% | +8.27% |
| D→C: code only, MRR272 | +4.17% / +4.57% | +4.37% |
| A→C: code + capacity | +10.87% / +10.52% | +10.70% |

The combined gain is measured directly, not a sum of individual percentages. Capacity/combination pairs span the two temporal blocks and do not have the same interleaving as the within-block code comparison. Two repetitions support this hardware/workload only; they are not a broad statistical performance guarantee.

The exact saved parameter bytes were also verified in the full model. At MRR512, logged loaded weights decrease 195.81→191.96 GiB/GPU and logical KV capacity increases 14,364,672→15,559,680 tokens (+8.32%); per-GPU KV storage increases 46.24→50.08 GiB. Under DCP8, log allocation slots are per-GPU, while `max_total_num_tokens` is logical aggregate capacity. Thus memory savings permit a larger running batch, but do not remove the projection/communication latency cost.

All eight runs complete without request failure, OOM, CUDA/scheduler error, or KV retraction. Latency must be assessed alongside throughput; the strict numerical gate remains unresolved. These exact-version results replace the earlier prototype evidence and do not inherit its +10.93% claim.

<details>
<summary>Native service and client arguments</summary>

Use the selected source checkout and an independent copy of the common tactic seed for each run. Model/output paths below are placeholders; tuning arguments are the recorded native arguments.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python"
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4
RUN_CACHE=/path/to/run/cache
export SGLANG_CACHE_DIR="$RUN_CACHE/sglang"
export TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RUN_CACHE/inductor"
export TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RUN_CACHE/triton"
export TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR="$RUN_CACHE/torch"
export FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE="$RUN_CACHE/flashinfer"
export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE=1
unset NCCL_ALGO NCCL_SYM_CTAS NCCL_SYM_KERNEL NCCL_SYM_CE_THRESHOLD NCCL_SYM_TMA_ENABLE
unset SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_SCHEDULER SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_OPERATIONS
ulimit -n 65536
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \
  --tp-size 8 \
  --dcp-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend fi_a2a \
  --context-length 69632 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.97 \
  --mm-feature-transport cpu \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
  --disaggregation-mode decode \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend fake \
  --disaggregation-decode-extra-slots 16 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --num-reserved-decode-tokens 1024 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --watchdog-timeout 1000000 \
  --log-level info \
  --enable-metrics \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":8}' \
  --tokenizer-worker-num 32 \
  --detokenizer-worker-num 32 \
  --max-running-requests 512 \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --flashinfer-autotune-skip-ops trtllm_batch_decode_mla \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 32 64 96 128 160 192 224 256 288 320 352 384 416 448 480 512
```

For the 272 groups, set `--max-running-requests 272` and `--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 32 64 96 128 160 192 224 256 272`; all other launch arguments stay the same.

```bash
ulimit -n 65536
aiakperf -r sglang -a 127.0.0.1:30000 \
  -m /path/to/Kimi-K3 -d random -if 65536 -of 1024 \
  -n 2048 -w 512 -cores 16 -seed 42 -temperature 0 -igr -stream \
  --fake-bootstrap -p 50,99 -v -o /path/to/run/formal
```

Warmup uses 512 requests with otherwise identical load arguments and separate output/data-cache paths. Reproduction must also retain the deterministic request-ID/bootstrap-room adaptation described above.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Changed-file Ruff, Ruff format, isort, codespell, clang-format and `git diff --check` pass.
- [x] Extend existing registered tests; CPU and eight-GPU runs pass.
- [x] Describe scope and workspace lifetime in code; no new user-facing option.
- [x] Run complete-model real-KV correctness/quality and matched service performance experiments on the exact candidate.
- [ ] Resolve the failed predeclared strict numerical gate or agree on numerical acceptance with maintainers before merging.
- [x] Follow existing linear/loading and collective implementations.

Local operator, full-model and service experiments are separate from upstream CI. The previous CI run stopped at **Block draft PR**, before the `run-ci` label check and model tests; it was not an operator-test failure. The PR is now ready for review and CI, with numerical acceptance still unresolved. Upstream tests require the `run-ci` label.

| A→C: code + capacity | +10.87% / +10.52% | +10.70% |

The combined gain is measured directly, not a sum of individual percentages. Capacity/combination pairs span the two temporal blocks and do not have the same interleaving as the within-block code comparison. Two repetitions support this hardware/workload only; they are not a broad statistical performance guarantee.

The exact saved parameter bytes were also verified in the full model. At MRR512, logged loaded weights decrease 195.81→191.96 GiB/GPU and logical KV capacity increases 14,364,672→15,559,680 tokens (+8.32%); per-GPU KV storage increases 46.24→50.08 GiB. Under DCP8, log allocation slots are per-GPU, while `max_total_num_tokens` is logical aggregate capacity. Thus memory savings permit a larger running batch, but do not remove the projection/communication latency cost.

All eight runs complete without request failure, OOM, CUDA/scheduler error, or KV retraction. Latency must be assessed alongside throughput; the strict numerical gate remains unresolved. These exact-version results replace the earlier prototype evidence and do not inherit its +10.93% claim.
